decisions.quote: We conducted a replication of the eight choosing versus rejection problems in Shaﬁr (1993). We successfully replicated the results of Problem 4 and Problem 5 of the original study. However, in Problems 7 and 8 we found eﬀects in the direction opposite to the original ﬁndings and our ﬁndings for Problems 1, 2, 3, and 6 indicated support for the null hypothesis.
decisions.reason: The paper re-tests all eight problems (Experiments 1–8) from Shafir (1993) and explicitly reports that two successfully replicated, four supported the null, and two showed opposite effects, which is coded as mixed under the codebook rules for multiple tested findings from the same original paper that come out differently.

decisions.quote: To test the accentuation hypothesis, we conducted binary logistic mixed-eﬀects regression analysis. In this analysis, we included responses from Problem 1 to 7, as these problems shared the common procedure of choosing between two alternatives (binary choice set). We followed Wedell’s (1997) approach to calculate the overall proportion of subjects (across experimental conditions) preferring the enriched alternative for each of the seven problems, as a measure of the overall relative attractiveness of the enriched alternative.
decisions.location: Section 3.5 Extension: Testing the accentuation hypothesis, p. 48
decisions.reason: Inspection of the title, abstract, introduction (Sections 1.1 and 1.2), method (Section 2.3), results (Section 3.5), discussion (Section 4.1), and reference list confirms that Shafir (1993) is the sole empirical target article re-tested in this replication. All eight decision scenarios and experimental stimuli were taken exclusively from Shafir (1993) (Section 2.3, p. 42). The paper never states any empirical finding, study, sample, or effect from Wedell (1997) to compare against; rather, it introduces Wedell (1997) as proposing a theoretical resolution (the accentuation hypothesis) of the conflicting findings between Shafir (1993) and Ganzach (1995) (Section 1.2, p. 40) and applies Wedell's (1997) analytical procedure—calculating overall enriched-option preference across conditions and running binary logistic mixed-effects regressions alongside new continuous attractiveness ratings—to the responses from Problems 1–7 of Shafir (1993) as an extension (Section 3.5, pp. 48–50; Section 4.1, p. 53). Under the codebook (Step 2 and Step 3 Rule 2), applying an analytical approach or testing agreement with a theoretical account on another target's stimuli without re-testing a stated published empirical finding of that work does not make Wedell (1997) a replication target.

decisions.quote: We tested the competing theoretical assertion by Wedell (1997). Our results in support of this account suggest that the stimuli from the 1990s are still of relevance, at least for testing that account.
